keyframe_review.note: 8,669 km2. The page has no area. The shape covers Salzburg and, by the gazetteer, the Berchtesgaden circle, with its bounding box running to 49.25 N, which fits the Eichstätt and Passau parts the page says were added; the Salzburg region alone is about 6,575 km2, so the rest is Berchtesgaden and the added bishopric lands. Unverified beyond that.
8,487 km2 (-182 km2 on 1803; the page gives no reason). The shape stands for the last year; the Pressburg transfer of 26 December 1805 is the dissolve event.

ledger.note: 11 February 1803: Salzburg passes from its archbishop to Archduke Ferdinand. The infobox dates the secularization of the archbishopric to February 11, 1803 and the article says Colloredo 'formally resigned in favour of Ferdinand on 11 February 1803'; the Etruria page adds that Ferdinand III 'was compensated with the Electorate of Salzburg' for his lost Tuscany.

27 April 1803: Salzburg is raised to an Electorate. The infobox gives the electorate's elevation as April 27, 1803; the Recess page says Salzburg 'was secularized as a duchy with an increased territorial scope, and was also made an electorate'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

1803: Berchtesgaden is added. The electorate was 'Augmented by the Berchtesgaden Provostry and parts of the former prince-bishoprics of Eichstätt and Passau'. The page gives the augmentation without a month; April follows the Recess becoming law on 27 April. Berchtesgaden is absent from the gazetteer, so it is a 15 km circle.

ledger.note: 1803: pieces of Eichstätt. Same sentence as above ('parts of the former prince-bishoprics of Eichstätt and Passau'). The page does not say which parts; the 30 km circle round Eichstätt is a placement, and the Cliopatria shape (to 49.25 N) shows detached lands to the north-west. The Eichstätt dossier dates its mediatisation to Salzburg 1802.

ledger.note: 1803: pieces of Passau. Same sentence. The Passau dossier gives the city and the left bank of the Inn to Bavaria and the rest to Salzburg; the Recess page lists Passau under the Elector of Bavaria, a conflict left unresolved, so the 20 km circle is a placement only.

26 December 1805: the Electorate of Salzburg ceases. 'the Salzburg electorate was dissolved by the Peace of Pressburg', 'signed on 26 December 1805'; the former archbishopric and Berchtesgaden pass to Austria, to be 're-established in 1806 as the Austrian Duchy of Salzburg'.

notes: Both Cliopatria shapes are kept as ok because no page gives an area; they include Berchtesgaden and detached lands as far north as 49.25 N, which fits the Eichstätt and Passau parts the page says were added. The state starts on 11 February 1803 (secularization and Colloredo's resignation) and is raised to an electorate on 27 April 1803 (rename event). Counterparts are the dossiers other agents have written (prince-archbishopric-of-salzburg, prince-provostry-of-berchtesgaden, prince-bishopric-of-eichstatt and -passau). The Recess page lists Passau under the Elector of Bavaria and not under Salzburg; the Salzburg page says parts of Passau were added to Salzburg in 1803 and annexed by Bavaria in 1805. The Austria side is austrian-empire although Cliopatria's Habsburg row (to 1805) is the owner on 26 December 1805: the Austrian Empire row starts in 1806 and carries the land. Berchtesgaden is absent from the gazetteer and appears as a coordinate circle.
